scenario: CHW home visit after discharge for sickle cell vaso-occlusive crisis; mother present, return to work, transport
text: Okay this is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Renata Okafor]], community health worker with Cadence, dictating a face to face home visit. Member is [[NAME:Darnell Whitfield]], last name spelled [[NAME:W H I T F I E L D]], date of birth [[DOB:March ninth nineteen ninety-six]]. Visit was the morning of [[DATE:October second]] at his apartment, [[ADDRESS:fourteen twelve Larchmont Avenue, apartment three B]], in [[CITY:Dayton]], [[STATE:Ohio]], [[ZIP:four five four oh six]]. Member I D is [[MEMBER_ID:C A D seven seven one, four zero two, nine nine]]. His mother [[RELATIVE_NAME:Loretta]] was there the whole visit, she does most of the pill box setup. Um, so [[NAME:Darnell]] was discharged from [[FACILITY_NAME:Saint Anselm's]] on [[DATE:the twenty-sixth]] after a four day admission for vaso-occlusive crisis, mostly low back and both thighs. He rates pain at a four out of ten now, it was a nine on admission. Meds reviewed with the bottles in hand, hydroxyurea one thousand milligrams daily, folic acid one milligram daily, oxycodone five milligrams every six hours as needed, he has six tablets left out of twelve, and he's been taking ibuprofen on top of that which I flagged, he needs to run that by hematology because of his kidney numbers. Vitals, blood pressure one eighteen over seventy-two, pulse eighty-eight, temp ninety-eight point four, sat ninety-seven percent on room air. He says he's drinking two liters a day, [[RELATIVE_NAME:Loretta]] rolled her eyes at that. Hematology is with [[PROVIDER_NAME:doctor Priya Raman]]. He aged out of [[FACILITY_NAME:Riverbend Children's]] a couple years back and now goes to [[FACILITY_NAME:Hilltop Hematology Associates]] over on [[ADDRESS:Wayne Avenue]]. Follow up with [[PROVIDER_NAME:doctor Raman]] is [[DATE:next Thursday]] at one fifteen. He wants to get back to work at [[EMPLOYER:Greenline Fuel and Market]], he's a shift lead, he's been out since [[DATE:the eighteenth]]. I'll fax the return to work form once [[PROVIDER_NAME:Raman]] signs off. His car is down so I booked a Medicaid ride, confirmation [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:R T four four eight, two zero nine]]. Mom's cell for reminders is [[PHONE:nine three seven, five five five, zero one six two]]. He's had four crises in the past year, up from two the year before. We talked through triggers, cold snaps, dehydration, stress, and he agreed to try the pain coping group that meets Wednesday evenings. Plan, hydration log, keep the hematology appointment, phone check in two weeks, and I'll look into a sickle cell peer support line for him. Flu shot is due, he declined for now. End of dictation.

scenario: RN post-op home visit three weeks after sleeve gastrectomy; husband present, daughter on speaker, MRN self-correction
text: This is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Marisol Tran]], R N care manager, dictating a post op home visit for [[NAME:Geraldine Pomeroy]], she goes by [[NAME:Gerri]], date of birth [[DOB:July twelfth, nineteen seventy-one]]. Her M R N at [[FACILITY_NAME:Lakeshore Bariatric Institute]] is [[MRN:L B I two two zero eight, no sorry, two two zero nine one four]]. She had a laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy with [[PROVIDER_NAME:doctor Anand Kulkarni]] on [[DATE:September fifteenth]], so about three weeks out. Husband [[RELATIVE_NAME:Walt]] was there and their daughter [[RELATIVE_NAME:Kayla]] called in on speaker partway through from work. They're out on [[ADDRESS:Birchwood]], the yellow ranch just past [[GEOGRAPHIC_CONTEXT:the Dollar General on Route nine]], in [[CITY:Racine]], [[STATE:Wisconsin]]. Weight two forty-one, down from two sixty-eight pre op. Five port sites, clean, dry, intact, the left upper one is a little pink, no drainage, no warmth. She's moving from full liquids to pureed, she's getting maybe fifty grams of protein a day, goal is sixty to eighty, so we went over the shakes again and sipping not gulping. Meds, omeprazole forty milligrams daily, ursodiol three hundred milligrams twice a day for gallstone prevention, chewable multivitamin twice a day, calcium citrate five hundred milligrams three times a day, B twelve sublingual, and levothyroxine eighty-eight micrograms for her Hashimoto's. Metformin was stopped at discharge and fasting sugars are running one oh five to one twenty. Blood pressure one thirty-four over eighty-two, pulse seventy-six, afebrile. She had nausea [[DATE:Saturday]] after trying scrambled eggs too early, that resolved, no vomiting. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Walt]] asked when she can go back to [[EMPLOYER:Harbor Point Credit Union]], she's a teller there, and the surgeon's note says light duty at four weeks, so that would be [[DATE:around the thirteenth]]. Next post op visit is with [[PROVIDER_NAME:Kulkarni]]'s P A, [[PROVIDER_NAME:Joelle Fournier]], on [[DATE:the twenty-eighth]]. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Kayla]] wanted to know about the support group, it meets the first Tuesday of every month in the evening, I gave her the flyer info. Best callback is [[NAME:Gerri]]'s cell, [[PHONE:two six two, five five five, zero one three eight]]. Plan, protein log, watch the left port site, reinforce vitamins for life, call [[DATE:Friday]] to check on the pureed transition. Okay that's it.

They're staying at her mom's place on [[ADDRESS:Delancey]] near [[GEOGRAPHIC_CONTEXT:the old Ferro Works lot]] in [[CITY:Toledo]]. Plan, weekly check ins, help with a bus pass, follow up on the hep C results, and I'll call [[DATE:Wednesday]] to see if the roofing job came through.

Pediatrician is [[PROVIDER_NAME:doctor Felicia Okonkwo-Hart]] at [[FACILITY_NAME:Eastside Pediatrics]], last seen in [[DATE:July]], follow up there [[DATE:the fifteenth]] at three forty. Medicaid I D for [[NAME:Amari]] is [[MEMBER_ID:nine eight two, two zero four, seven seven one, five]], mom read it off the card. Mom works nights at [[EMPLOYER:Garden State Packaging]], so text is better than calling, her cell is [[PHONE:nine seven three, five five five, zero one zero six]]. Plan, order the second spacer, request a HEPA filter through the home environment benefit, send a copy of the asthma action plan to the school, flu shot at the [[DATE:fifteenth]] visit, and recheck peak flows by phone in one week.

Wife [[RELATIVE_NAME:Ingrid]] is the primary caregiver and son [[RELATIVE_NAME:Peter]] joined by video from [[CITY:Minneapolis]]. Function, he's on the eye gaze device most of the time now, speech is mostly unintelligible, he typed tell them I'm fine, which got a laugh. BiPAP at night and now about four hours in the afternoon, I PAP fourteen, E PAP six. F V C at the last clinic was forty-one percent predicted. Meds, riluzole fifty milligrams twice a day crushed per tube, glycopyrrolate one milligram three times a day for secretions, baclofen ten milligrams three times a day, sertraline fifty milligrams daily. Neurologist is [[PROVIDER_NAME:doctor Samuel Achterberg]] at the [[FACILITY_NAME:Crestwood]] neuromuscular clinic, they see him every three months, next one is [[DATE:the ninth of November]]. Equipment, power chair from [[ORGANIZATION:Prairie Mobility Supply]], the tilt function is broken, ticket number [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:P M S dash zero zero four eight one seven]]. Ceiling lift is working. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Ingrid]] is exhausted, she's up two or three times a night for suctioning. We talked about hospice again and [[NAME:Hal]] spelled out not yet, but he agreed to a palliative care consult. He also said through the device that he wants his old buddies from [[EMPLOYER:Heartland Implement]] to come by, he worked there thirty-one years. Advance directive on file, D N R, the POLST is on the fridge. Respite, waiver hours are eight a week, I'm requesting twenty. Contact is [[RELATIVE_NAME:Ingrid]]'s cell, [[PHONE:six four one, five five five, zero one two seven]]. I'll call her [[DATE:Monday]] about the palliative referral and the chair.

scenario: Face to face visit for moderate Alzheimer's dementia after an overnight wandering episode found by police; daughter and son-in-law present
text: Face to face, this is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Bettina Ruiz-Calloway]] with Cadence. She told the officer she was going to her shift at [[EMPLOYER:Minnesota Valley Telephone]], which is where she worked as an operator for, I think, twenty-some years. No injuries, mild hypothermia, they checked her at the E D and sent her home. Diagnosis is Alzheimer's, moderate, MoCA was twelve out of thirty in [[DATE:June]]. Meds, donepezil ten milligrams at bedtime, memantine ten milligrams twice a day, melatonin three milligrams, and she's on amlodipine five. Her Medicare number is on the fridge, [[MEMBER_ID:four F J seven, H R two, N C one eight]], I updated our file. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Karen]] lives in [[CITY:North Mankato]], about ten minutes away, her cell is [[PHONE:five oh seven, five five five, zero one nine three]]. We talked about memory care, they put her name on the waitlist at [[FACILITY_NAME:Bluff Ridge]] memory care but it's months out. Plan, caregiver respite hours, adult day expansion, medication lock box, and recheck in two weeks.

scenario: Member summary: adult with Down syndrome in a group home with new cognitive decline; sister is guardian
text:
Member Summary - [[NAME:Benjamin Oyelaran]] ("[[NAME:Benji]]")
DOB [[DOB:02/03/1982]] | Medicaid [[MEMBER_ID:IA-DD-0773914]] | Waiver case [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:55-20174]] | Cadence CM: [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Theo Mancini]]

[[NAME:Benjamin]] is a 44-year-old man with Down syndrome who has lived at [[FACILITY_NAME:Maple Hollow Residence]], a four-bed group home on [[ADDRESS:Thornbury Lane]] in [[CITY:Cedar Rapids]], since 2015. His sister and legal guardian, [[RELATIVE_NAME:Adaeze Oyelaran-Pike]], lives in [[CITY:Des Moines]] and visits about once a month; she prefers updates by email at [[EMAIL:adaeze.pike@example.org]]. The home manager, [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Carla Peterson]], is the day-to-day contact at [[PHONE:(319) 555-0145]].

Medical: hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 125 mcg (TSH 6.8, recheck pending); obstructive sleep apnea on CPAP, average use 5.2 h/night; right cataract extraction in 2021; recurrent cerumen impaction. Over the past 8 months staff have noticed new forgetfulness, getting turned around in the house at night, and less interest in his job bagging groceries at [[EMPLOYER:Hometown Fresh Market]], which he has held for nine years. A dementia screen (NTG-EDSD) was completed by [[PROVIDER_NAME:Dr. Imani Oduya]] at [[FACILITY_NAME:Linn County Developmental Clinic]], and neurology is booked for [[DATE:Nov 12, 2026]].

What matters to [[NAME:Benji]]: country music, his Saturday bowling league, and calling his sister on Sunday nights. He communicates in short sentences and some sign, and does best with visual schedules.

Goals: rule out reversible causes (thyroid, hearing, sleep); maintain employment with job coach support; caregiver training for staff on early dementia signs.

scenario: Narrative member summary: older veteran with Parkinson's disease, PTSD and recurrent falls; wife caregiver, daughter POA out of state
text:
Member summary: [[NAME:Lawrence Riordan]], DOB [[DOB:3/15/1949]], MA member ID [[MEMBER_ID:H5521-0398814]]

[[NAME:Mr. Riordan]] is a 77-year-old Army veteran who served in Vietnam and later spent 28 years as a welder at [[EMPLOYER:Pelican State Ironworks]]. He lives with his wife, [[RELATIVE_NAME:Patricia]] ("[[RELATIVE_NAME:Pat]]"), in a single-story home at [[ADDRESS:1023 Quail Hollow Drive]], [[CITY:Bossier City]], [[STATE:Louisiana]]. Their daughter, [[RELATIVE_NAME:Moira Kent]], lives in [[CITY:Houston]] and holds financial and medical power of attorney.

He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in 2018 and follows with [[PROVIDER_NAME:Dr. Celestine Thibodeaux]] at [[FACILITY_NAME:Red River VA Clinic]]. He takes carbidopa/levodopa 25/100, 1.5 tabs five times daily, and reports wearing-off about 3 hours after each dose. He has fallen three times since [[DATE:July]]; the most recent fall, on [[DATE:Sept 28]] in the garage, led to an ED visit at [[FACILITY_NAME:Northwest Louisiana Regional]] with no fracture. PTSD-related nightmares are improved on prazosin 2 mg at bedtime. Orthostatic BP at last visit was 138/80 sitting, 112/70 standing.

[[RELATIVE_NAME:Pat]] does most of the caregiving and says she is "tired but managing." She prefers email ([[EMAIL:patriordan@example.net]]); the home phone is [[PHONE:(318) 555-0117]]. Cadence CM is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Marcus Delacroix-Webb]].

Priorities: fall prevention (PT home safety eval, grab bars, garage lighting), medication timing review with neurology, caregiver respite for [[RELATIVE_NAME:Pat]], and confirming [[RELATIVE_NAME:Moira]]'s POA paperwork is on file with the clinic.

scenario: Narrative timeline of postpartum hemorrhage followed by postpartum depression and anxiety; FMLA, mother visiting
text:
Timeline narrative - [[NAME:Keisha Monroe]], Medicaid [[MEMBER_ID:SC 7731 2048 85]]

[[NAME:Keisha]] delivered her second child at [[FACILITY_NAME:Lowcountry Women's Hospital]] on [[DATE:June 11, 2026]] by repeat C-section, complicated by postpartum hemorrhage (EBL 1,600 mL) requiring 2 units PRBCs. She went home on [[DATE:June 14]] with her husband, [[RELATIVE_NAME:Andre]], and the baby, [[RELATIVE_NAME:Jalen]].

On [[DATE:June 20]], Cadence maternal CM [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Felicity Amankwah]] made the first home visit at [[ADDRESS:509 Magnolia Bend Road]], [[CITY:Summerville]]. Hgb was 8.9, BP 136/88, incision intact; EPDS 8. Iron sucrose infusions were arranged.

By [[DATE:mid-July]] things had changed: at the [[DATE:July 16]] call her EPDS was 16, she was not sleeping even when the baby slept, and she described intrusive thoughts about something happening to him, with no intent to harm. Same day, a warm handoff went to [[PROVIDER_NAME:Dr. Rachel Zimmerman]] at [[FACILITY_NAME:Harbor Behavioral Health]], who started sertraline 50 mg. Her mother, [[RELATIVE_NAME:Gloria Monroe]], came up from [[CITY:Savannah]] to stay for three weeks.

Her planned return to work at [[EMPLOYER:Palmetto Freight Brokers]] on [[DATE:August 4]] was postponed under FMLA (claim [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:FML-77302-K]]). Over [[DATE:Labor Day weekend]] she went to the ED at [[FACILITY_NAME:Lowcountry]] with chest tightness; troponin negative, evaluated as a panic attack. Sertraline was increased to 100 mg on [[DATE:September 18]], and EPDS dropped to 9.

At her OB follow-up with [[PROVIDER_NAME:Dr. Pickett]] on [[DATE:October 2]], she reported sleeping 5-6 hours and enjoying time with the kids again. Postpartum Medicaid coverage continues for 12 months. Best contact: [[PHONE:843-555-0174]]. Next CM check-in is planned for the week she returns to work.
